motivation: Pre-loss focal history predicts whether Thalassia is re-recorded and, in a separate endpoint, predicts stability after re-recording. Recovery-debt analysis shows returned points are quantitatively depressed. Test whether focal local history also predicts the quantitative depth of recovery.

source.history_definition: same focal Thalassia run and generic habitat-headstart decomposition as results/focal_vs_habitat_legacy_v1_contract.json

primary_population.pattern: Thalassia present at t, absent at t+1, present at t+2

history_decomposition.thalassia_run: immediately consecutive consensus years ending at source year with Thalassia present
history_decomposition.any_seagrass_run: immediately consecutive consensus years ending at source year with any seagrass present
history_decomposition.centering: thalassia_run and habitat_headstart centered by stable-node means among eligible recovered sequences

primary_hypothesis.statement: Among recovered exact points, longer-than-usual focal Thalassia persistence history predicts higher return-year Braun-Blanquet state after source abundance, generic habitat headstart, loss-year vegetation continuity, source mixture, stable node, and return year are represented.
primary_hypothesis.direction: positive coefficient = deeper quantitative recovery with longer focal history
primary_hypothesis.support_rule: lower bound of 95% node-bootstrap interval for thalassia_run_centered coefficient > 0

secondary: centered habitat-headstart coefficient and bootstrap interval
return-year Braun-Blanquet mean by integer pre-loss Thalassia run length where >=10 sequences occur
source-to-return Braun-Blanquet change by pre-loss run-length class, descriptive only

interpretation.supported: Local focal persistence history predicts not only return probability but the quantitative depth of re-recorded recovery, consistent with path-dependent recovery quality.
interpretation.unsupported: Focal history predicts whether or how stably Thalassia returns but does not robustly predict return-year quantitative abundance after current source state and habitat-history controls; recovery quality is a distinct dimension.

claim_boundary: Post-hoc quantitative recovery endpoint on an already-opened exact-point return dataset.
A positive history coefficient would not prove clonal memory, residual rhizomes, carbohydrate reserves, or genet survival.
Braun-Blanquet is ordinal abundance, not percent cover, biomass, or ecosystem function.
Generic habitat headstart and stable-node controls reduce but do not eliminate unmeasured microsite quality.
Return is recorded reappearance at the same meter mark, not proven recolonization.
Do not change history decomposition, centering, source-state control, loss-year state, quantitative inclusion, model, minima, or support threshold after opening recovery quality by history.
